Subject: Questions on log pruning timeline & evidence for SOC2/SIG

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our compliance team has a couple of follow-ups before we finalize the private deployment onboarding:

- We need explicit maximum retention windows (in days) for the following artifacts scoped to our tenant: session logs (request/response traces), debug traces (full stack/diagnostic dumps), and any persistent KV-cache snapshots that could contain user data.
- For SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ purposes they want to know what proof-of-delete looks like from Redwood (what artifacts you provide to demonstrate deletion took place).
- If we request a tenant-specific shorter retention window (e.g., 30d for debug traces), what is the operational lead time and what evidence will you provide once the shorter window is applied and data is purged?

Can you send an evidence pack (or checklist) that we can pass to our auditors that lists: retention defaults, configurable options for private deployments, typical proof-of-delete artifacts, and the expected turnaround for producing those artifacts?

We attached a short spreadsheet with the questions the SOC2 reviewer passed along.

Appreciate a reply with specific windows and the timeline (we're aiming to close this by next Friday).

Best,

Diego / Priya,

Below is a concise draft of what we can commit to for a private (VPC) deployment. This is based on our current Private product capabilities and our SOC2 evidence pack. I've attached the relevant excerpts.

Proposed retention defaults and tenant-scoped minima (can be tightened per contract):
- Session logs (request/response traces): default 60 days; configurable down to 14 days for tenant-scoped policy. Session logs are indexable for troubleshooting; we can apply retention rules that delete tenant indexes and underlying objects.
- Debug traces (full stack / extended diagnostics): default 90 days; configurable down to 30 days. Debug traces are stored as transient debug buckets and are not included in long-term telemetry exports unless explicitly enabled.
- KV cache: No long-term persistent snapshots by default. KV cache entries are in-memory or on-GPU/ephemeral backing stores and subject to eviction; we do not persist full KV snapshots to persistent blob storage for private deployments unless the customer requests an export. If CardioScan requests strict non-persistence, we can document and sign that policy.

Proof-of-delete / evidence artifacts we can produce:
- Proof-of-delete audit log: service-side deletion events for tenant IDs (timestamped).
- Erasure job output: execution logs from the deletion run (file list, checksums if applicable).
- Object-store delete receipts (if objects were removed from storage buckets).
- Configuration snapshot: copy of the retention policy applied and the effective timestamp when it was enforced.
- Optional: a signed attestation letter from Redwood legal confirming the deletion scope and time window.

Operational notes and lead times:
- Applying a tenant-specific retention change: typical lead time is 3 business days to schedule and apply, 5 business days if a manual data purge is requested in addition to policy change.
- Evidence pack turnaround: 5 business days after purge completion to assemble and deliver the artifacts.

Recommended response to customer: ask them to confirm the target retention windows (we recommend 14/30/30 as a more conservative starting point: session logs 14d, debug traces 30d, KV non-persistence), and whether they want a signed attestation. Once they confirm we can provide a canonical mutual action plan and produce the evidence pack after purge.

Attachments I've included: retention_playbook_excerpt.pdf (excerpt of internal retention playbook), kv_cache_notes.md (engineering note on cache persistence).

Happy to help craft the message to CardioScan.

—Marissa
Sr. Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference

Hi Helen / Alex —

Thanks for the detailed ask and the spreadsheet. Below is our proposed answer and a short mutual action plan so your SOC2 reviewer has concrete dates. Marissa copied in the exact artifacts we can provide.

What we can confirm today (private/VPC deployment):
- Session logs: default 60 days; we can apply a tenant-scoped policy down to 14 days.
- Debug traces: default 90 days; configurable down to 30 days.
- KV cache: no automatic long-term snapshots; KV entries are ephemeral/evicted. We do not persist complete KV snapshots to long-term blob storage by default.

Proof-of-delete we will deliver after any agreed purge:
1) Proof-of-delete audit log (tenant ID + timestamps of deletion operations).
2) Erasure job output (execution log with file/object identifiers).
3) Bucket/Object delete receipts where applicable.
4) Configuration snapshot showing the retention policy change and effective timestamp.
5) Optional signed attestation letter from Redwood legal (template attached).

Mutual action plan (suggested):
- By EOD 2027-09-02: CardioScan confirms target windows and whether you want the signed attestation. (Suggested conservative starting windows we recommend: session logs 14d, debug traces 30d.)
- By 2027-09-06: Redwood schedules and applies tenant-scoped retention policy change (if requested).
- By 2027-09-09: If a manual purge is requested, Redwood completes purge operations.
- By 2027-09-14: Redwood delivers evidence pack (audit logs, erasure output, delete receipts, configuration snapshot; attestation if requested).

Attachments for your review: redwood_erase_checklist.xlsx (checklist of artifacts we'll produce), retention_playbook_excerpt.pdf. Also linking our internal playbook excerpt here: https://drive.redwood.com/RetentionPlaybook/tenant-pruning-guidance.pdf.

If that timeline works, I'll schedule the policy change and loop in operations to start the work. If your compliance team needs different artifact formats (e.g., checksums, signed timestamps), let us know in your confirmation and we'll include that in the pack.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Account Solutions
Redwood Inference
